service.description: What the database db allows the Tools screens, and why the rest is not available ("needs the pg_monitor role", "pg_stat_statements is not loaded"), probed once and kept five minutes; refresh probes again. features maps each of statementStats, activity, cancel, terminate, lockWaits, tableSizes, bloatExact, indexUsage, indexOnline, fkLightLock, maintenance, integrity, settings, settingsEdit and backups to available and reason (why not, or what limits it). backend is embedded-postgres, postgres, mysql or mariadb. available is false, with reason, when the database did not answer.

Forget the entity facade's statement stats of this instance (entity-facade@query-stats), as ec.entity.clearQueryStats() does. Needs the DATABASE_ADMIN permission, and writes a DbaStatsReset DatabaseAudit row.

Compare the entity model with the database (EntityDbMeta::compare): missing tables, missing, extra and differently typed columns, missing, extra and invalid indexes, missing and extra foreign keys, and on Postgres foreign keys no index leads with. entityNames empty compares every entity of the group. tables lists only the tables with a difference, each with entityName, groupName, tableName, missingTable, missingColumns, extraColumns, columnTypes, missingIndexes (with their ddl), extraIndexes, invalidIndexes, missingForeignKeys (with ddl), extraForeignKeys and unindexedForeignKeys.

The statements that bring a selection of the comparison's differences in line, in the online forms (§5.2): on Postgres CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS, DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS, ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, and an invalid index dropped and created again (REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY for one the model does not have); on MySQL ALGORITHM=INPLACE LOCK=NONE. changes is some of missingIndexes, invalidIndexes, extraIndexes (dropped), missingForeignKeys, extraForeignKeys (dropped) and dropForeignKeys (every key of the selected tables); empty is missingIndexes, invalidIndexes and missingForeignKeys. names limits the plan to these index and key names (one row). Each statement has statementSeqId, statementText, dependsOnSeqId, entityName, tableName, what and lockTimeout (whether it takes the job's lock timeout); create#DatabaseJob takes the list as it is.

The DDL of entityNames (every entity of the group when empty) in the database's dialect, from the builders the table check uses: CREATE TABLE (with the full-text columns), then the indexes, then the foreign keys among the selected entities; for Download DDL as fileName.

A DatabaseJob of statements on db (§6), Pending, and run on a service worker unless run is false. statements is a list of maps (statementText, and statementSeqId and dependsOnSeqId as plan#SchemaChanges gives them) or of texts, or one script text that is split into its statements. lockTimeoutMs bounds the wait for a strong lock (default 5000; CONCURRENTLY and VALIDATE statements wait as long as they need). Needs DATABASE_ADMIN.

Run the job jobId here, or run it again: its statements not Done run in order, each on a connection of its own outside a transaction with no statement timeout, its backend id on its row. A statement with a strong lock waits at most the job's lock timeout and is tried three more times; one whose dependsOnSeqId did not finish is DbjsSkipped; a failed one does not stop the others. An invalid index a failed CONCURRENTLY build left is dropped before the build runs again. At the end the job is DbjsDone, DbjsFailed (a statement failed or was skipped) or DbjsCancelled, its user is notified on topic DatabaseJob, a summary is logged and a DbaJob DatabaseAudit row written. create#DatabaseJob calls it on a worker. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN.

Cancel the job jobId: it is marked DbjsCancelled so no further statement starts, and its running statement is cancelled, with the canceller of this instance when it runs here (how local), else by its backendPid with pg_cancel_backend or KILL QUERY on a connection of its own (how backend). A job not started is how notStarted; one that ended is cancelled false, how none. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaCancel DatabaseAudit row.

The job jobId (its DatabaseJob fields), its statements (DatabaseJobStatement fields), and for a statement running now the server's progress (Postgres pg_stat_progress_create_index, _vacuum and _analyze; MySQL performance_schema.events_stages_current; MariaDB the PROCESSLIST progress) and the sessions blocking it (pg_blocking_pids joined to pg_stat_activity). A Running job of an instance that is gone is marked DbjsFailed ("the server stopped") on the first jobs call after a start.
The latest database jobs, newest first, of statusId when given.

Each table's estimated rows, total, table and index bytes, live and dead rows, last vacuum, autovacuum, analyze and autoanalyze, sequential and index scans (Postgres), or the InnoDB estimates, free bytes and update time (MySQL), largest first, from one catalog query, each with entity_name. reason is the error when the query failed.
The exact row count of the table tableName (one the schema has).

The statements of a maintenance job on tableNames: action vacuumAnalyze (VACUUM (ANALYZE)), analyze, reindex (REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY), vacuumFull and cluster on Postgres, which take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and need allowExclusiveLock; analyze (ANALYZE TABLE) and optimize (OPTIMIZE TABLE) on MySQL and MariaDB. Out as plan#SchemaChanges; run with create#DatabaseJob and kindEnumId DbjMaintenance.

The database's sessions (Postgres pg_stat_activity of this database; MySQL and MariaDB the PROCESSLIST) with state, wait event, query and transaction start and statement, each marked own_app (this instance's, by the application_name the drivers set to the instance id), idle_in_transaction_long (over a minute), running_long (over ten seconds), with blocked_by; and blockingChains, trees of pid and blocks from the sessions that wait on no one.
Cancel the statement of session pid (pg_cancel_backend, KILL QUERY). signalled is whether the server found the session. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaCancel DatabaseAudit row.
End session pid (pg_terminate_backend, KILL). Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; writes a DbaTerminate DatabaseAudit row.

The index checks of §4.2: unindexedForeignKeys (Postgres: keys no index leads with), unusedIndexes (not unique, never scanned since statsSince), duplicateIndexes (led by another index of the table, with covered_by), invalidIndexes (a failed CONCURRENTLY build), and the transaction id wraparound ages databaseAge and tableAge (Postgres).
